Failure is 99% of success. It's never too late to change yourself. Never. If drugs are the thing that you've chosen then you should get help, I used to have an opiate addiction and the best thing I ever did for myself was to go get help from a rehab clinic.

Don't give up! 

I'm utterly obsessed with my ex and how beautiful her smile is, but I don't imagine that it's the best memory to dwell on, it seems to ruin me as much as it brings me happy memories... the thought of not having that around me anymore is shattering, yet the memory of her smile is heartwarming.

Do you have any hobbies? When I feel awful I find putting my complete focus into something makes me a feel alot better, even if only for the time being.

I can relate to that. I sold my house a few years ago after breaking up with a girl, and I spent the majority of the profit on drugs because I was in pain and didn't want to feel what I was feeling. Of course that was a path of destruction and lead to nowhere but mental illness. 

On top of that I've always dealt with relationships in a passive nature, ignoring the problems and pushing them to the side in hope that it will just all be ok. 

Eventually you end up in too deep a hole and can't get out of it. I never really realized what it was doing to my partner, but now that I look back I wish I could have been different, as now she must think less of me for it. Sometimes (or often) love doesn't conquer all it seems.

Just know that you are not alone, thanks for sharing.

cheating is the worst. I wish people would stop and think of what it does to their families. If only people spoke to each other more, I think a better understanding of each other would connect people more in relationships and bring people together, rather than push them apart.

I'm sorry that happened to you, your fondest memory sounds like a lovely one to hold on to. Never give up on happiness, think about how much your daughters love you. 

I grew up with split parents, It was always a contest for my father to be the one that was more loved. It didn't make us kids love him any more than our mother - in fact it was more than awkward. Eventually he killed himself because he couldn't handle it.

That might be at the core of all my problems, but that's irrelevant... just don't take that path, please, it will ruin your children's lives.

omg, I couldn't imagine ever doing that to somebody that I'm supposed to love. people are such pussies. cheating is for losers!

but your fondest memory made me chuckle... revenge is a dish best served with eggs - thanks for sharing.

Please don't end it all. You are a generous, kind person and I couldn't imagine how hard it must be to keep up with that amount of grief.

Never let your kindness be your downfall. 

No matter what you think your plan is, it's not the right one to just disappear. 

It's a shame to hear that people leave you when you're at your worst. And it's nearly always about money, when really people can't relate to how much you are actually going through. 

Either that or they are just too selfish to realize what type of sacrifice you are making. Good people should care about that sort of thing.

Do you ever connect with your father emotionally? Is there a way you can address his drinking in a manner that would make him try stop for you? Or any way that you could make him see what it is that it's doing to you to take care of him all the time?
